cases.prompt: set up my new mac for development
i just unboxed a macbook pro - take it from zero to ready to code
fresh macos install, make me a full dev environment
walk me through a complete developer setup on this mac
new work laptop, need everything: shell, git, runtimes, docker, the works
make this mac dev-ready end to end
wiped my mac, restore a full development environment from scratch
set up this machine for mobile web and ai development, all of it
set up zsh with a nice prompt
generate an ssh key for github
set up my mac for ios development
show hidden files and speed up key repeat
Brand new MacBook - set it up for development. I do web and a bit of cloud work.
expected_behavior: inventories existing state first (brew? git? xcode-select? existing shell config?) instead of assuming factory-fresh

proposes a plan: core sequence (system-prep, security, homebrew, zsh, cli-tools, git identity, runtimes, defaults, editor, dotfiles) plus the web and cloud optional tracks - and asks the user to confirm/trim BEFORE installing anything
applies the modern default stack (Starship, mise+uv, VS Code+Cursor) while preserving any existing shell/runtime setup it detects
executes each area via its focused skill's workflow in dependency order, verifying after each step and stopping on failures rather than plowing on
does not install unrequested optional tracks (mobile, ai) and ends with a whole-machine verification summary listing manual steps left (App Store sign-in, FileVault, license keys)

cases.prompt: take this mac from zero to fully ready, i want everything including mobile and the ai clis
expected_behavior: still plans first: shows the full track list with rough disk/time costs (Xcode ~40-50GB) and confirms
sequences correctly: system prep before homebrew, homebrew before everything brew-based, runtimes before mobile extras, defaults/dotfiles at the end
asks the subtrack questions (iOS/Android/both, which cloud providers, which AI CLIs) rather than installing all
runs verification at the end and reports every manual step remaining

cases.prompt: my mac is half set up already - brew exists, git works. finish the job to a complete dev environment
expected_behavior: detects and preserves the existing setup (does not reinstall brew or regenerate ssh keys), diffing plan vs reality
proposes only the missing areas and confirms
verification covers pre-existing pieces too (brew doctor, ssh -T) to catch latent breakage
